bounded_proposition: Boot-MBR start/size sector counts are narrowed from guint64-derived values to guint32 without a visible range check at the narrowing site.
direct_source_fact: Region and boot-switch quantities are carried as guint64 bytes; get_raw_partition_entry stores divided sector start/size in guint32 MBR fields.
inferred_consequence: Reachable sector values above G_MAXUINT32 could change under narrowing.
falsifying_or_downgrading_evidence: Find a frozen-source invariant or documented bound proving every reachable MBR sector start/size <=G_MAXUINT32.
b1_schema_reason: Exact duplicate proposal P07-01 merged into P01-01 mechanism.

bounded_proposition: A guint64 boot-switch partition byte size is cleared using a guint byte counter.
direct_source_fact: dest_partition->size is guint64; clear_count is guint and advances by write return counts.
inferred_consequence: For reachable sizes above G_MAXUINT, the counter cannot monotonically represent all bytes to the target.
falsifying_or_downgrading_evidence: Find a reachable-size bound <=G_MAXUINT or supported ABI evidence that guint is 64-bit.

bounded_proposition: Region-end validation forms a guint64 sum of start and size without an explicit pre-addition overflow guard.
direct_source_fact: Both operands are guint64 and are directly added before boundary checks.
inferred_consequence: A mathematically out-of-range sum could wrap before comparison.
falsifying_or_downgrading_evidence: Find parser/config bounds proving all reachable sums fit guint64.

bounded_proposition: Any negative NBD netlink disconnect send result is normalized to local cleanup and TRUE return.
direct_source_fact: The failure branch logs 'already removed' without discriminating error cause, clears state, and returns TRUE.
inferred_consequence: Non-benign send errors could be collapsed into successful/already-complete removal semantics.
falsifying_or_downgrading_evidence: Establish kernel/libnl contract or documented RAUC best-effort API semantics eliminating the distinction.

bounded_proposition: Stored checksum size is read without an error channel when a digest is present.
direct_source_fact: The size getter is called with NULL error handling while checksum digest/type remain populated.
inferred_consequence: Malformed/missing size may survive as a numeric fallback alongside a digest.
falsifying_or_downgrading_evidence: Establish GLib behavior plus downstream usage showing no source-level consequence or prove storage writer invariants exclude malformed external input.

bounded_proposition: Activation can return success despite failure to persist activation metadata after the bootloader primary change succeeds.
direct_source_fact: Status persistence errors are logged/freed and do not convert the operation to failure.
inferred_consequence: Caller-visible success and persisted activation metadata can diverge.
falsifying_or_downgrading_evidence: Find an explicit best-effort/non-authoritative persistence contract or guaranteed retry path.

bounded_proposition: Polling second values accepted as gint are multiplied in gint arithmetic before assignment to gint64 milliseconds.
direct_source_fact: No upper bound beyond gint range is checked; *1000 and default *4 are evaluated on gint operands.
inferred_consequence: Large accepted intervals can exceed intermediate signed-int representation.
falsifying_or_downgrading_evidence: Establish a frozen bound or language/toolchain behavior preventing overflow for all accepted values.

bounded_proposition: The binary-suffixed numeric parser neither validates the whole token nor checks the scaled left-shift result.
direct_source_fact: After g_ascii_strtoull it examines only *scale and returns result<<scale_shift.
inferred_consequence: Malformed trailing text may be accepted; scaled values may wrap.
falsifying_or_downgrading_evidence: Find an upstream canonical-token/range validator covering every call.
b1_schema_reason: Parent candidate retained at B1; B3 may split tail-validation and scaling-overflow children only if frozen split criteria are met.

bounded_proposition: Normal polling backoff multiplies a signed interval by an incremented guint64 error count before applying the configured maximum.
direct_source_fact: The multiplication precedes MIN and uses signed/unsigned operands of the cited widths.
inferred_consequence: At sufficiently large counts the pre-clamp expression may not represent intended mathematical backoff.
falsifying_or_downgrading_evidence: Establish conversion semantics and a reachable-state bound that precludes overflow/wrap before the clamp.
